text:
DENSE-METRIC CEILING - a defensible bound now, with the precise measurement deferred. Also a correction to my own method.

METHOD CORRECTION. I began measuring the ceiling by shrinking active_slices and extrapolating linearly in node count. That design is invalid, and I caught it before publishing a number. Reducing slices TRUNCATES the searchlights, so support size changes with node count:

  slices= 1  nodes=  2184  mean k = 12.6   (k/k_full)^3 = 0.055
  slices= 2  nodes=  4368  mean k = 21.3   0.269
  slices= 3  nodes=  6552  mean k = 24.9   0.429
  slices= 8  nodes= 17472  mean k = 29.4   0.705
  slices=24  nodes= 52416  mean k = 31.2   0.842

The dominant per-support cost is a k-by-k solve, so it scales roughly as k^3. Extrapolating linearly from a 1-slice fixture would have understated the per-node cost by about 18x and produced a wildly optimistic ceiling. Any ceiling measurement must hold support size fixed, or normalise by k^3 explicitly. Discarding those numbers.

BOUND THAT NEEDS NO NEW COMPUTATION. The gate itself is the measurement. At 52416 nodes with mean k = 31.2 it has consumed more than 45 minutes and has not finished. Holding k fixed, cost is close to linear in node count, so a 30-minute budget corresponds to at most

  52416 * 30/45 = 34944 nodes

and because the run is still going the true figure is lower. So the supported dense-metric ceiling at this support size is BELOW roughly 35000 nodes, and that is a generous upper bound rather than an estimate.

WHY I AM NOT MEASURING MORE PRECISELY RIGHT NOW. The gate worker is saturating a core. Timing measurements taken under that contention would be unreliable, which is the same class of error as the extrapolation above - I would be measuring the machine, not the code. The precise ceiling should be measured on a quiet machine, at fixed active_slices = 24 with reduced in-plane extent so k stays near 31, at two or three node counts.

PRACTICAL RECOMMENDATION FOR EPIC 8 IN THE MEANTIME: the scope statement does not need the exact ceiling to be useful. "Brain-scale diagonal metrics supported; dense local metrics not supported at whole-brain node counts, measured ceiling below ~35000 nodes at support size ~31, exact boundary to be pinned on a quiet machine" is honest, actionable, and already better than a pass at a degenerate fixture would have been.
